entries.name: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
entries.abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.

entries.name: Functional weak convergence of stochastic integrals for moving averages and continuous-time random walks
entries.abstract: There is an extensive theory of weak convergence for moving averages and continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) with respect to Skorokhod's M1 and J1 topologies. Here we address the fundamental question of how this translates into functional limit theorems in the M1 or J1 topology for stochastic integrals driven by these processes. As an important application, we provide weak approximation results for general SDEs driven by time-changed Lévy processes. Such SDEs and their associated fractional Fokker--Planck--Kolmogorov equations are central to models of anomalous diffusion in statistical physics. Our results yield a rigorous functional characterisation of these as continuum limits of the underlying models driven by CTRWs. With regard to strictly M1 convergent moving averages and correlated CTRWs, it turns out that the convergence of stochastic integrals can fail decidedly and fundamental new challenges arise compared to the J1 setting. Nevertheless, we identify natural classes of integrand processes for which there is M1 convergence of the stochastic integrals. We also show that these results are flexible enough to yield functional limit theorems in the M1 topology for certain stochastic delay differential equations driven by moving averages.

entries.name: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
entries.abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomassé. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.

entries.name: Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions
entries.abstract: We enumerate the numbers $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324)$ of 1324-avoiding $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ inversions for all $k$ and $n \geq (k+7)/2$. The result depends on a structural characterization of such permutations in terms of a new notion of almost-decomposability. In particular, our enumeration verifies half of a conjecture of Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson, according to which $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324) \leq \mathrm{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)$ for all $n$ and $k$. Proving also the other half would improve the best known upper bound for the exponential growth rate of the number of $1324$-avoiders from $13.5$ to approximately $13.002$.

entries.name: Well-posedness and long-time behavior for self-consistent Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equations with general potentials
entries.abstract: We study the well-posedness, steady states and long time behavior of solutions to Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation with external confinement potential and nonlinear self-consistent interactions. Our analysis introduces newly characterized conditions on the interaction kernel that ensure the local asymptotic stability of the unique steady state. Compared to previous works on this topic, our results allow for large, singular and non-symmetric interactions. As a corollary of our main results, we show exponential decay of solutions to the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation in dimension $3$, for low regularity initial data. In the repulsive case, the result holds in strongly nonlinear regimes (i.e. for arbitrarily small Debye length). Our techniques rely on the design of new Lyapunov functionals based on hypocoercivity and hypoellipticity theories. We use norms which include part of the interaction kernel, and carefully mix ``macroscopic quantities based''--hypocoercivity with ``commutators based''--hypocoercivity.

entries.name: A Computational Study for Solving Decision-Dependent Robust Problems as Bilevel Optimization Problems
entries.abstract: Both bilevel and robust optimization are established fields of mathematical optimization and operations research. However, only until recently, the similarities in their mathematical structure has neither been studied theoretically nor exploited computationally. Based on the recent results by Goerigk et al. (2025), this paper is the first one that provides an extensive computational study for solving strictly robust optimization problems with decision-dependent uncertainty sets as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. If the uncertainty set can be dualized, the respective bilevel techniques to obtain a single-level reformulation are very similar compared with the classic dualization techniques used in robust optimization but lead to larger single-level problems to be solved. Our numerical study shows that this usually leads to larger computation times. For the more challenging case of decision-dependent uncertainty sets represented by mixed-integer linear models, one cannot apply classic dualization techniques from robust optimization. Thus, we compare the presented bilevel approach with an established method from the literature, which is based on quantified mixed-integer linear programs. Our numerical results indicate that, for the problem class of decision-dependent robust optimization problems with mixed-integer linear uncertainty sets, the bilevel approach performs better in terms of computation times.

entries.name: Fourier transform of nonlinear images of self-similar measures: quantitative aspects
entries.abstract: This paper relates to the Fourier decay properties of images of self-similar measures $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^k$ under nonlinear smooth maps $f \colon \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}$. For example, we prove that if the linear parts of the similarities defining $μ$ commute and the graph of $f$ has non-vanishing Gaussian curvature and $κ_2 > k/2$, then the Fourier dimension of the image measure is at least $\frac{2(2κ_2 - k)}{4 + 2κ_* - k}$, where $κ_2$ is the lower correlation dimension of $μ$ and $κ_*$ is the Assouad dimension of the support of $μ$. Under some additional assumptions on $μ$, we use recent breakthroughs in the fractal uncertainty principle to obtain further improvements for the decay exponents. We give several applications to nonlinear arithmetic of self-similar sets $F$ in the line. For example, we prove that if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (\sqrt{65} - 5)/4 = 0.765\dots$ then the arithmetic product set $F \cdot F = \{ xy : x,y \in F \}$ has positive Lebesgue measure, while if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (-3 + \sqrt{41})/4 = 0.850\dots$ then $F \cdot F \cdot F$ has non-empty interior. One feature of the above results is that they do not require any separation conditions on the self-similar sets.

entries.name: When majority rules, minority loses: bias amplification of gradient descent
entries.abstract: Despite growing empirical evidence of bias amplification in machine learning, its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. We develop a formal framework for majority-minority learning tasks, showing how standard training can favor majority groups and produce stereotypical predictors that neglect minority-specific features. Assuming population and variance imbalance, our analysis reveals three key findings: (i) the close proximity between ``full-data'' and stereotypical predictors, (ii) the dominance of a region where training the entire model tends to merely learn the majority traits, and (iii) a lower bound on the additional training required. Our results are illustrated through experiments in deep learning for tabular and image classification tasks.

entries.name: The Solver's Paradox for SAT
entries.abstract: We show in Rocq that every circuit verifier $v$ determines a formula $ψ_v$ whose satisfiability is $v$'s acceptance of its own diagonal claim: a satisfiability predicate thus behaves like a provability predicate. Every solver represented in the language misclassifies its own diagonal instance, and every verifier misjudges its own diagonal claim. We distinguish our result from (i) the refuters of Chen et al. (2024), which produce from the description of a solver an instance it gets wrong, and (ii) the refuter of Gutfreund et al. (2007) for efficient SAT solvers, which needs a hardness hypothesis and a simulation. Here the refuter is purely syntactic, and it separates evaluation of the language from its own expressions, not SAT from a resource-bounded class. The identity behind the fixed point uses no property of quotation; its reading as self-reference depends on the coding, and an injective recoding flips the branch. A truth table decides $ψ_v$ only from outside the language. Written inside, it is brute force: it settles the claim from above and has a diagonal instance of its own. This yields an unconditional certification hierarchy with tower growth, a quadratic lower bound on every internal evaluator, and an exponential lower bound on brute force.

entries.name: On the connectedness of a minimizing cluster's boundary
entries.abstract: We verify that an isoperimetric minimizing cluster on a simply connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with at most one end always has connected boundary. In particular, the boundary of a single-bubble isoperimetric minimizer on such manifolds must be connected, and hence all isoperimetric sets and their complements must be connected. This is demonstrably false without the simple connectedness assumption or the restriction on the number of ends.

entries.name: Stochastic Deep Learning: A Probabilistic Framework for Modeling Uncertainty in Structured Temporal Data
entries.abstract: I propose a novel framework that integrates stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with deep generative models to improve uncertainty quantification in machine learning applications involving structured and temporal data. This approach, termed Stochastic Latent Differential Inference (SLDI), embeds an Itô SDE in the latent space of a variational autoencoder, allowing for flexible, continuous-time modeling of uncertainty while preserving a principled mathematical foundation. The drift and diffusion terms of the SDE are parameterized by neural networks, enabling data-driven inference and generalizing classical time series models to handle irregular sampling and complex dynamic structure. A central theoretical contribution is the co-parameterization of the adjoint state with a dedicated neural network, forming a coupled forward-backward system that captures not only latent evolution but also gradient dynamics. I introduce a pathwise-regularized adjoint loss and analyze variance-reduced gradient flows through the lens of stochastic calculus, offering new tools for improving training stability in deep latent SDEs. My paper unifies and extends variational inference, continuous-time generative modeling, and control-theoretic optimization, providing a rigorous foundation for future developments in stochastic probabilistic machine learning.

entries.name: Kantorovich Distance via Spanning Trees: Properties and Algorithms
entries.abstract: We study optimal transport between probability measures supported on the same finite metric space, where the ground cost is a distance induced by a weighted connected graph. Building on recent work showing that the resulting Kantorovich distance can be expressed as a minimization problem over the set of spanning trees of this underlying graph, we investigate the implications of this reformulation on the construction of an optimal transport plan and a dual potential based on the solution of such an optimization problem. In this setting, we derive an explicit formula for the Kantorovich potential in terms of the imbalanced cumulative mass (a generalization of the cumulative distribution in R) along an optimal spanning tree solving such a minimization problem, under a weak non-degeneracy condition on the pair of measures that guarantees the uniqueness of a dual potential. Our second contribution establishes the existence of an optimal transport plan that can be computed efficiently by a dynamic programming procedure once an optimal spanning tree is known. Finally, we propose a stochastic algorithm based on simulated annealing on the space of spanning trees to compute such an optimal spanning tree. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed approach for optimal transport on finite metric spaces.

entries.name: The non-ergodic Host-Kra-Ziegler structure theorem for $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions via measurable selections
entries.abstract: We establish a non-ergodic version of the Host--Kra--Ziegler structure theorem for measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions. Our argument reduces the non-ergodic case to the ergodic theorem (for $d\ge 2$ due to Candela and Szegedy) via a measurable selection procedure. We also establish a non-ergodic vertical nilcharacter version of our main result. The non-ergodic version of the Host--Kra--Ziegler structure theorem is a key input in the companion paper by the second author and Fraczyk classifying point processes (i.e. random subsets) of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ whose law is invariant under the group $\mathrm{ASL}_d(\mathbb{Z})$ of affine transformations.

entries.name: Gödel-Tarski Translation for Constructive Logics with Transitive Closure
entries.abstract: We introduce the semantically-defined constructive propositional dynamic logics of regular programs $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$, respectively extending the basic constructive modal logic $\sf CK$ and its Wijesekera-style variant $\sf WK$. Using translations between our logics and $\sf PDL$, we show that both $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$ are {\sc ExpTime}-complete and enjoy an exponential-size finite model property. In particular, their diamond-free fragment, restricted to a single atomic program and its reflexive transitive closure is already {\sc ExpTime}-complete, thereby settling the conjecture of Afshari et al. By embedding $\sf CS4$ and $\sf WS4$ into our logics, we show their validity problems are also in {\sc ExpTime}, improving the previously known {\sc NExpTime} upper bound obtained via finite model arguments.

entries.name: On the Chevalley-Bass number of a field
entries.abstract: We give upper and lower bounds on the Chevalley-Bass number of a field of characteristic zero, whenever this quantity is well-defined. We also describe an algorithm which computes the Chevalley-Bass number of a field, provided its maximal abelian subextension is known. As a primary application, we improve the value of a constant related to exponential Diophantine equations.

entries.name: Involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction
entries.abstract: We determine all involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction that extend the involution of the original $*$-algebra. We also find all algebra isomorphisms between the resulting Cayley doubles that extend the identity automorphism of the original $*$-algebra, and consequently classify the resulting $*$-algebras up to such $*$-algebra isomorphisms. As applications, we show that Cayley doubles of algebras without zero divisors admit exactly one additional extension of the original involution in the 2-torsion-free case and none otherwise, prove that the classical Cayley-Dickson involution is the unique scalar involution, and obtain a classification of the $*$-algebras arising from $\mathbb{R}$ up to dimension 4.

entries.name: Nilpotent quiver varieties with multiplicities and symmetrisable crystals
entries.abstract: We construct analogues of Nakajima's nilpotent quiver varieties for quivers with multiplicities, by developing new stability conditions for framed nilpotent quiver representations with multiplicities and exploiting their interplay with Hecke correspondences. Using these new quiver varieties, we extend Saito's geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals of irreducible highest-weight representations of Kac--Moody algebras from the symmetric to the symmetrisable case.

entries.name: Multilevel limits of spiked random matrix corners processes
entries.abstract: We consider the largest eigenvalues of submatrices of the classical Gaussian random matrices with a finite rank spike in the critical BBP regime. We show that they converge to a multilevel interlacing particle system whose lowest level is the Airy$_β$ point process. Our construction and scaling limits extend in a natural way to non-classical $β>0$.

entries.name: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
entries.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-Kähler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.

entries.name: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
entries.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

entries.name: Bias Correction and Inference for Panel Quantile Regression
entries.abstract: We develop a large-$n$, large-$T$ theory for the unsmoothed fixed-effects quantile regression estimator that allows for serially correlated panel data. An exact rank-score identity for the profiled criterion, with a convexity argument, delivers the leading incidental parameter bias of the slope estimator, of order $T^{-1}$, in closed form, paralleling Hahn and Newey (2004) for smooth nonlinear panel models. When $n$ and $T$ grow at the same rate, the estimator is asymptotically normal but in general not centred, and conventional intervals are invalid. In stationary panels whose dependence decays geometrically or polynomially, with $n/T$ bounded, serial correlation changes the structure of this bias: the long-run variance of the quantile score enters it, and feedback from past errors to current regressors adds a term that can bias the estimator even at the median. A split-panel jackknife with contiguous half-panels removes the bias, whereas one with interleaved half-panels does not in general, and a cluster-robust variance estimator, clustered by individual, yields valid inference. Under independence over time, the admissible growth of $n$ relative to $T$, up to $n=o(T^3)$, depends on the regularity of the conditional error densities, and the jackknife is valid throughout this range.

entries.name: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
entries.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.

entries.name: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
entries.abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

entries.name: On the solution of a question for meromorphic functions sharing three values IM and a fourth value CM in the complex plane
entries.abstract: In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a Möbius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

entries.name: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
entries.abstract: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.

entries.name: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
entries.abstract: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.

entries.name: Reflected Elastic Diffusions
entries.abstract: We study the reflected elastic diffusion (RED), the pathwise counterpart of Feller's elastic boundary condition for a one-dimensional diffusion on $[0,\infty)$ with time-homogeneous, continuous drift and diffusion coefficients. Given a diffusion $X$ reflecting at zero, we construct a Feller process $\widetilde X$ by killing $X$ at the first time its local time at zero exceeds an independent exponential random variable. We characterize the infinitesimal generator of $\widetilde X$ explicitly and prove that its domain satisfies a Robin boundary condition, thereby identifying $\widetilde X$ as a probabilistic representation of Feller's analytical characterization of the elastic boundary. A key analytical ingredient, of independent interest, is a pair of moment asymptotics, as $t\downarrow 0$, for the boundary local time of a reflected diffusion, extending known results for the unreflected case. Uniqueness in law of $\widetilde X$ among Feller REDs sharing the same interior dynamics is established through a resolvent/boundary-value-problem argument. The result extends the classical Itô-McKean construction of elastic Brownian motion to time-homogeneous diffusions, closing the gap between analytic and probabilistic treatments of elastic killing used in recent applied models.

entries.name: Linear forms in logarithms of rational numbers: an ineffective measure with the best possible exponent
entries.abstract: Let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be positive rational numbers without a nontrivial multiplicative relation. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $C>0$, not effective, such that $|h_0+h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n| \ge C\max(1,|h_0|,\dots,|h_n|)^{-n-\varepsilon}$ for all integers $h_0,\dots,h_n$, not all zero. The exponent $n$ is best possible. For $n=1$ this is the known fact that the irrationality exponent of $\log a$ is $2$; for $h_0=0$ it gives the exponent $n$ for the linear forms $h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n$. The proof is an induction on $n$, starting from $n=1$. The step from $n-1$ to $n$ logarithms uses an interpolation determinant on $\mathbb{G}_m^n\times\mathbb{G}_a$ at the multiples of a rational point, in the manner of arXiv:2610.28079; its geometric part, a curve inequality, is proved by a second induction, on the number of torus coordinates, with the two-torus inequality of arXiv:2610.28079 as the base. The method is the interpolation and determinant method of OpenAI's preprint on the irrationality exponent of $π$; the case $n=1$ was obtained earlier by Liu, Jiang and Zhang (arXiv:2610.10192). The theorem and its corollary are verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the sources are in the ancillary files, on top of the Lean supplement of arXiv:2610.28079. This paper follows the formal proof: every definition, constant and intermediate statement is given in the form in which it is formalized, with the name of the Lean declaration.

entries.name: On Cohen Generic Sets in Supercompact Prikry Extensions
entries.abstract: Let $κ$ be $λ$-supercompact for a regular $λ>κ$. We show that if $λ$ is not the successor of a singular of cofinality below $κ$, $\diamondsuit(S^λ_{\geqκ})$ implies that every ${<}κ$-strategically closed forcing of size at most $λ$ is a projection of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing. We show that the situation for successors of singulars of small cofinality is independent. Finally, we provide more limitations about the class of $κ$-distributive projections of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing and give examples of $κ$-distributive forcings of size $λ$ which cannot be projections of this forcing.

entries.name: On convergence rate bounds for Markovian push-sum algorithms
entries.abstract: In this work we establish an upper bound on the almost sure convergence rate of a broad class of push-sum algorithms, more precisely for those where message passing events follow a Markovian dynamics, or a Hidden Markov Model. In this context, having a computationally accessible quantity at hand is of top priority; we thus formulate tools to cut down the complexity of obtaining the stated bound. Furthermore, we introduce a transformation to adjust a given push-sum scheme in a way that the bound on the rate provably improves -- and often so does the true convergence rate. Theoretical understanding is complemented by numerical results, where the quality of all three directions is demonstrated: for the bound on the rate, for the computational complexity and for the improvement strategy.

entries.name: A geometric-IEQ approach for curvature-driven flows
entries.abstract: We introduce a geometric invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) formulation for the $L^2$-gradient flow of a class of curvature-dependent energies of closed hypersurfaces, where the energy density depends on the mean curvature and the unit normal. A square-root auxiliary variable converts the geometric energy into a quadratic functional. Combining its evolution equation with a skew-symmetric treatment of surface transport yields a weak formulation whose energy law depends only on the normal velocity and is therefore independent of the chosen tangential motion. We construct monolithic nonlinear parametric finite element methods by coupling a common IEQ discretization with one of two geometric formulations that accommodate either the Barrett-Garcke-Nürnberg (BGN) tangential velocity or the minimal-deformation-rate (MDR) tangential velocity. Both fully discrete approximations satisfy an unconditional decay estimate for the discrete quadratic energy. We further extend the construction to anisotropic Willmore flow, and to $H^{-1}$-gradient flows. A variety of numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the robustness and accuracy of the introduced methods.

entries.name: Disc functionals and rational curves
entries.abstract: We prove a criterion for the existence of rational curves on compact Kähler manifolds using disc functionals. As applications, we obtain a transcendental version of the Miyaoka--Mori theorem with an optimal degree bound and a new proof of the characterization of uniruled compact Kähler manifolds.

entries.name: Unique continuation and its failure for the Monge--Ampère equation
entries.abstract: We study unique continuation for Alexandrov solutions with common Monge--Ampère density bounded above and below. In the plane, we prove that agreement on an open set forces global equality. For every bounded domain \(Ω\subset\mathbb R^n\) with \(n\ge3\), we construct two distinct uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}(Ω)\) solutions that agree on a nonempty open subset of \(Ω\).

entries.name: On the Geometry of Quadratic Maps
entries.abstract: To analyse a homogeneous quadratic map $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^\ell$, the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ of its restriction to the unit sphere is very useful but difficult to handle. We prove its dual hypersurface $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is of degree $k$ (providing its equation) and is $\mathit{hyperbolic}$: every line though the origin in $\mathbb{R}^\ell$ cuts it at $k$ real points, counting multiplicities. These facts imply: $\boldsymbol{1}$. $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is the union of $k/2$ nested topological hyperspheres if $k$ is even, or the union of $(k-1)/2$ nested topological hyperspheres and one topological projective hyperplane if $k$ is odd. $\boldsymbol{2}$. The Toeplitz-Haussdorf Theorem on the range of of the restriction of $Q$ to the unit sphere if $k>\ell$. $\boldsymbol{3}$. The dual version of the hyperbolicity of $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is: the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ is of class $k$. $\boldsymbol{4}$. For generic $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^k$, $Σ_{Q}$ contains $\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\rfloor$ collections of ellipsoids of codimension $2$ consisting of degenerate parabolic points. $\boldsymbol{5}$. If $k>\ell$, the parabolic set in $Σ_{Q}$ (if any) is a union of hyperplane closed discs bounded by ellipsoids. $\boldsymbol{6}$. The above ellipsoids (items $4$ and $5$) are in bijection with the isolated singular points in $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$.

entries.name: Strong Banach property $(T)$ for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$
entries.abstract: Strong Banach property $(T)$ has been established for higher-rank algebraic groups over non-Archimedean local fields with respect to Banach spaces of nontrivial type. However, in the real setting, existing results have required additional geometric hypotheses on the Banach spaces, leaving the corresponding question open even for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$. We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$ has strong Banach property $(T)$ with respect to every class of complex Banach spaces of uniformly nontrivial Rademacher type.

entries.name: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
entries.abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urbański in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to choose a single pair of potential coefficients that controls both possible separating gaps. The dimension formula remains valid after excluding trivially singular matrices.

entries.name: On the theorem of F. Riesz on Blaschke products and on inner functions in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^{n}
entries.abstract: For a convergent Blaschke product $f$ in the unit disc of $\mathbb C$, let $G(f)$ be the set of all points $t$ on the unit circle for which $|f(rt)| \rightarrow 1$ as $r \rightarrow 1$. By a classical F. Riesz theorem $G(f)$ is of full measure, which describes $G$ metrically. We describe $G$ topologically by proving that it is a $G_δ$ set. The same description is true in general for inner functions not only in the unit disc but also in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^n$.

entries.name: Lessons from Chess: Mathematics in the Age of AI
entries.abstract: The history of chess offers a perspective on the growing role of artificial intelligence in mathematics. We explore the parallels and limitations of this analogy and consider possible directions for mathematical research, education, and the public perception of mathematics.

entries.name: Compactness-like properties in Alexandroff paratopological groups
entries.abstract: We study compactness-like and covering properties in non-compact Alexandroff paratopological groups. Several properties are characterized in terms of the order structure associated with the Alexandroff topology and the number of connected components. We establish equivalences among $2$-pseudocompactness, countable $o$-compactness, Baire, and an intersection property for increasing chains. We also obtain a common characterization of $σ$-local compactness, $σ$-compactness, the Lindelöf property, and left $ω$-precompactness in terms of the existence of a countable cofinal subset. Moreover, we characterize pseudocompactness, $H$-compactness, star-compactness, the countable chain condition, and the weakly Lindelöf property by means of the number of connected components. Finally, we determine further implications among the properties considered and provide examples and counterexamples.

entries.name: Sharp signature-weighted total-curvature bounds for complete minimal submanifolds
entries.abstract: Let $i:M^n\to\R^{n+p}$ be a complete connected minimal immersion, with $n\ge3$. We get a sharp bound of $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ$ from below in terms of the number of ends and the mod-two Betti numbers of $M$. As an application, if $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ<γ_n$, then $i(M)$ is an affine $n$-plane. Moreover, if $\int_M |A|^n\ddμ=γ_n$, then $i(M)$ is an $n$-catenoid in an affine $(n+1)$-plane, where $γ_n=\frac{[n(n-1)]^{n/2}}{n-1}\Vol(\Sn^n)$.

entries.name: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
entries.abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\geκ$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $κ$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $κ$. If $κ>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.

entries.name: The spectrum of codegree Turán densities of 3-graphs
entries.abstract: The \emph{minimum codegree} $δ_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Turán density} $γ(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $δ_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $α\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Turán density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_α$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $γ(\mathcal{F}')>α$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_α$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Turán spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independently of us.) We also consider \emph{positive codegree Turán density}, defined analogously by taking the minimum only over $(k-1)$-sets contained in at least one edge. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c<1$ such that, for every integer $k\geq3$, every real number in $[c,1)$ is the positive codegree Turán density of a $k$-graph family. This is done by presenting a construction with a relatively short proof, without optimising the value of $c$.

entries.name: Hypergeometric Abelian Surfaces and Triangle-Group Levels
entries.abstract: We study three families of hypergeometric abelian surfaces with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We determine their integral homology lattices and monodromy, including the choice of lattice at the ramified prime above $5$ in the plus family. One family is isomorphic to an explicit quadratic twist of a genus-two Frey Jacobian, with the two real-multiplication embeddings exchanged. The specified isogeny is twice an isomorphism and has kernel equal to the full $2$-torsion. Each family gives two real rank-two representations, with projective local monodromies of order $5$ at two punctures and parabolic monodromy at the third. Exactly one of the six projective representations is discrete, with image $Δ(5,5,\infty)$. Reduction at the two primes above $11$ gives six degree-$12$, genus-two covers parametrizing torsion lines. For the family with a discrete constituent, these Borel covers are the triangular modular curves $X_0(5,5,\infty;\mathfrak q)$; the comparison descends to ordered covers over $K$. The generic arithmetic projective image is $\PGL_2(\F_{11})$; the Galois closure of each Borel cover has constant field $K(\sqrt{-11})$.

entries.name: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
entries.abstract: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calderón-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.

entries.name: A hyperbolic 7-manifold that fibers over the circle
entries.abstract: We construct an explicit orientable finite-volume hyperbolic $7$-manifold $M$ that fibers over the circle. The manifold is tessellated by $256$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic polytope $P^7$ and has $252$ cusps. The fiber is the interior of a compact aspherical $6$-manifold whose boundary consists of $256$ five-dimensional tori. The fibration comes from a Bestvina-Brady Morse function on the Davis complex. Bestvina-Brady theory shows that the kernel of the associated character is finitely presented. A perturbation argument over the integral Novikov ring shows that the infinite cyclic cover is finitely dominated. Farrell's fibering theorem, together with the vanishing of the Whitehead group, then gives the fibration.

entries.name: Strong Subdifferentiability in Bochner Function spaces $L^{p}(μ, X)$
entries.abstract: In this article, for $1\leq p<\infty$, we provide a characterization of strongly subdifferentiable points of $L^{p}(μ, X)$, when $X^*$ is separable and $μ$ is the Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$. For $f\in L^{p}(μ, X)$ with $\|f\|_{p}=1$ we show that the norm of $L^{p}(μ, X)$ is strongly subdifferetiable at $f$ if and only if the norm of $X$ is strongly subdifferentiable at $f(t)$ for almost every \(t\in[0,1]\) with $f(t)\neq 0$. Moreover, for a separable Banach space $X$, we show that the norm of $L^{p}(μ, X)$ is strongly subdifferentiable if and only if the norm of $X$ is strongly subdifferentiable.

entries.name: Trace-class perturbations of Voiculescu's free semicircular families
entries.abstract: Let $\{s_j\}_{j\inΛ}$ be the standard free semicircular family on the full Fock space $\mathcal H=\mathcal F(\ell^2(Λ))$, where $|Λ|\geqslant2$. For any family $\{K_j\}_{j\inΛ}$ of self-adjoint trace-class operators with $γ=\sum_{j\inΛ}\|K_j\|_1<\infty$, we prove that the type $\mathrm{II}_1$ summand $\mathcal P$ of the von Neumann algebra $W^*(\{s_j+K_j\colon j\inΛ\})$ is isomorphic to the free group factor $\mathcal L(\mathbb F_Λ)$. As an application, we show that the set of irreducible operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is not dense in the trace-class norm. For each fixed $γ>0$, the possible values of the Murray--von Neumann dimension $\dim_{\mathcal P}(z_{\mathcal P}\mathcal H)$ form the interval $[1,1+γ)$, where $z_{\mathcal P}$ is the identity of $\mathcal P$.

entries.name: Wigner Matrices and the $α$-Determinant
entries.abstract: For a Hermitian Wigner matrix $M_n$ and complex $α$ with $|α|\leq1$, we study the $α$-characteristic polynomial $\det_α(zI-M_n)$, which interpolates between the characteristic polynomial ($α=-1$) and the permanental polynomial ($α=1$). Assuming finite fourth moments off the diagonal and second moments on it, we show that this polynomial, normalized by its expectation, converges in distribution off the segment $\sqrt{-α}\,[-2,2]$ to the Wick exponential of an explicit Gaussian analytic function, with the same Gaussian modes for every $α$. As consequences, all zeros lie near this segment with probability tending to one, the empirical zero measure converges to a rotated semicircle law, and analytic linear statistics of the zeros satisfy a central limit theorem. We also show that $\det_α(zI-M_n)$ is approximated, with vanishing relative error, in terms of the characteristic polynomial of $M_n$ at a transformed point. The proof writes the $α$-characteristic polynomial as a polymer gas, which becomes asymptotically ideal after an exact resummation over matchings.

entries.name: The Exact Value of the Rankin Number gamma_{5,2}
entries.abstract: The Rankin number gamma_{5,2} measures the exact upper bound for the squared determinant of the densest 2-dimensional sublattice of any 5-dimensional lattice of determinant one. We prove that gamma_{5,2}=16^{1/5}, attained by D*_5.

entries.name: A $(17/7-o(1))n$ Circuit Lower Bound for Binary-Encoded 3-SAT
entries.abstract: We strengthen the elementary $n-1$ circuit lower bound for a specified binary encoding of 3-SAT to $(17/7)n-O(n\log\log n/\log n)$ gates over the full two-input Boolean basis, with unrestricted depth and sharing. For each integer $w\ge5$, we encode 3-CNF formulas with exactly $m=2^w-1$ clauses over $m$ available variables using $n=3m(w+1)$ bits. The proof embeds Boolean tests in variable identifiers while retaining $n-o(n)$ free bits, and combines weighted gate elimination with a nonlinear-gate lower bound from the tests' full algebraic degree over $\mathbb F_2$. We provide Lean proofs of the finite inequality and the asymptotic bound for arbitrary acyclic binary circuits.

entries.name: The optimal exponent in the Erdős--Fuchs theorem for $k$-fold sums
entries.abstract: Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer. For an infinite set $A$ of nonnegative integers and a real number $x\ge0$, let $r_k(A,x)$ be the number of $k$-tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in A^k$ satisfying $a_1+\cdots +a_k\le x$. In this paper, we prove that $r_k(A,x)=cx+o(x^{(1-1/k)^2})$ is impossible for any real number $c>0$. The exponent $(1-1/k)^2$ is best possible for $k\ge3$ by a recent result of Guo and Yan. Moreover, we obtain a mean-square estimate of $r_k(A,x)-cx$ and confirm a conjecture of Chen and Tang for every $k\ge3$.

entries.name: A symmetric eigenvalue lower bound for Hadamard products
entries.abstract: For a positive semidefinite matrix $X$, let $μ_k(X)$ be the minimum of the least eigenvalues of its principal submatrices of order $k$. For positive semidefinite $A,B$ of order $n$, we prove \[ μ_{i+j-1}(A\circ B)\geqμ_i(A)μ_j(B), \qquad i,j\in\{1,2,\dots,n\},\quad i+j-1\leq n, \] and characterize equality when the right-hand side is positive. The resulting symmetric least-eigenvalue bound \[ λ_{\min}(A\circ B)\geq \max_{1\leq i\leq n}μ_i(A)μ_{n-i+1}(B) \] recovers the classical Schur lower bounds at endpoint choices and can be exact even when both factors are singular. It is incomparable with the projection bound from a recent companion paper, and combining the two bounds can improve on both. The proof combines a spectral minorant of $B$ whose diagonal entries are at least $μ_j(B)$ with the projection inequality underlying the companion bound. Multifactor and Khatri--Rao consequences are also given.

entries.name: The number of non-isomorphic spanning trees in regular graphs
entries.abstract: By a classical theorem of Otter, the number of non-isomorphic trees on $n$ vertices is $α^n\exp(-o(n))$, where $α\approx 2.956$ is Otter's constant. We prove that every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices contains $α^n\exp(-o_d(n))$ non-isomorphic spanning trees, where $o_d(n)/n\to0$ as $d\to\infty$.

entries.name: Metric structure in Hecke-induced modules for groups acting on buildings
entries.abstract: Let $X$ be a thick locally finite building of type $(W, S)$ and $G$ be a locally compact group acting properly and chamber-transitively on $X$. We give a condition on a Hermitian module $(V_0, \varphi_0)$ of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra $\mathbf C_{\mathbf q}[W]$ ensuring that the natural $G$-invariant form defined on the induced $G$-module has the same negative index as $\varphi_0$, where ${\mathbf q}$ is the thickness vector of $X$. It implies that induction of Hecke-modules preserves unitarity. In the affine case, this recovers results by Matsumoto, Barbasch--Moy and Ciubotaru. In general, assuming that $G$ is Weyl-transitive, we obtain new irreducible $G$-representations on Hilbert spaces as well as on infinite-dimensional symmetric spaces of finite rank. Using Hecke-modules of Lorentzian signature, we also derive new obstructions to Kazhdan's property (T), showing that the known sufficient conditions in terms of the thickness are mostly necessary.

entries.name: Eigenvector geometry and spectra of doubly stochastic matrices
entries.abstract: Let $U_N$ be the union of the convex hulls of the $k$th roots of unity for $1\le k\le N$. We prove that, for $N\ge10^{213}$, every convex combination of two permutation matrices of order $N$ has spectrum in $U_N$. The ordered pairs of columns selected in the rows form directed cycles. The proof uses the winding about the origin and the Fourier coefficients of the eigenvector coordinates along one cycle. For arbitrary doubly stochastic matrices, we form a polygon by assigning distinct columns to selected eigenvector coordinates. Near a root of unity of exact order $q\le N$, the full eigenvalue region agrees locally with the regular $q\lfloor N/q\rfloor$-gon. For $N\ge256$, suppose an eigenvalue lies outside $U_N$. In every associated eigenvector $v$ normalised by $\max_i|v_i|=1$, some coordinate $v_j$ lies strictly inside the convex hull of the coordinates and satisfies $|v_j|^2>1-100/N$.

entries.name: A Classification of Low Genus Modular Curves
entries.abstract: Let $G$ be an open subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\in G$. Associated to $G$, there is a modular curve $X_G$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ which parametrizes elliptic curves with $G$-level structure. We give a classification of modular curves with genus equal to a fixed nonnegative integer $g$. In particular, we show that all modular curves of genus $g$ lie in finitely many families of $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathrm{ab}}$-twists of modular curves. We also describe an algorithm for computing all families of modular curves of a fixed genus $g$ and use this to compute projective models for these modular curves. This algorithm has been fully implemented for $g \leq 12$. In an appendix with Yongyuan Huang and Rakvi, we describe two algorithms, one for computing rational functions on modular curves given as quotients of two modular forms of the same weight, and the other for computing models for the generic fibers of universal elliptic curves $\mathcal{E}_G$, where $G\subset \mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ is an open subgroup satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\notin G$.

entries.name: Uniform velocity support for the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system
entries.abstract: This paper proves that the velocity support of the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system remains uniformly bounded for all time for nonnegative initial data in \(C_c^1(\mathbb R^6)\). The proof establishes uniform bounds on a weighted fifth-order energy moment and an associated fourth-order force integral by exploiting the relative motion of particle pairs. On intervals where the target particle moves sufficiently fast relative to the expansion, these estimates give a summable bound for the current in its energy identity. This bound yields uniform control of the velocity support.

entries.name: The sharp Trudinger--Moser exponent in Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces
entries.abstract: We establish the sharp Trudinger--Moser inequality in the fractional Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces $W^{s,p}$, $0 < s < 1$, at the critical index $sp=N$, including the endpoint. More precisely, there exists a constant $C_{N,s}$ such that for every measurable set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ of finite positive measure, $$ \sup\Bigl\{\frac{1}{|Ω|}\int_Ωe^{α_{s,N}|u|^{\frac{p}{p-1}}}dx: u\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^N), u=0\text{ a.e. on }\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΩ, [u]_{s,p}\le 1\Bigr\}\le C_{N,s}, $$ where $[u]_{s,p}$ is the Gagliardo seminorm and $α_{s,N}$ is the upper threshold found by Parini and Ruf for $N\ge 2$ and by Iula for $N=1$. Moreover, the constant $α_{s,N}$ is sharp. This answers two of their questions. We use a nonlocal version of Moser's one-dimensional lemma. The $p$-th moment of a translation kernel on the logarithmic half-line determines the sharp coefficient, and finiteness of the next moment characterizes the endpoint. We obtain sharp singular, whole-space, Adachi--Tanaka type, concentration-compactness and affine inequalities. When the Euclidean distance in the seminorm is replaced by the gauge of an origin-symmetric star body $K$, we determine the sharp exponent for each fixed $K$ and show that it exceeds the volume-normalized exponent unless $K$ is an ellipsoid. The same exponents are sharp for regional seminorms on bounded Lipschitz domains in dimensions $N\ge 2$. We prove attainment of the critical supremum on balls for $N\ge 2$ and $s$ close to one. In the Hilbert case $N=1$, $s=1/2$, we compute the concentration level of the singular problem on an interval using a sharp weighted logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Consequently, the critical supremum is attained for every singular weight $|x|^{λ-1}$, $0 < λ\le 1$.

entries.name: Higher-Order Minkowski Inequalities via Gradient-Weighted Hessian Potentials
entries.abstract: We prove a sharp boundary inequality for exterior potentials of a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian equation under regularity, level-curvature, flux conservation, and radial decay hypotheses. The inequality bounds a power of the Newton flux by the normalized integral of $H_k^p/H_{k-1}^{p-1}$, and equality characterizes balls. After a conformal change of metric, two Newton-tensor divergence identities give comparisons between regular levels even when the slab between them contains critical points. For smooth strictly star-shaped domains with strictly $k$-convex boundary, a companion existence theorem supplies exterior potentials for $p$ close to one. We identify the limiting flux with the integral of $H_{k-1}$ and recover the sharp consecutive Minkowski inequality, including its equality case.

entries.name: Closed-Form Formula for $d_{\mathrm{critical}}(a_0)$ in Large Fully Connected Power Grids
entries.abstract: Kadloor and Santhi (arXiv:1011.4098) modeled cascading failures in a large fully connected power grid by a coupled four-variable recursion for the minimum surviving load $a_n$, the mean failed load $μ_{n-1}$, the redistributed load $\mathcal{D}_n$, and the stagewise failure probability $p_n$. They noted that the recursion was not tractable and identified the critical disturbance $d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ by simulation. We show that the recursion telescopes exactly into a one-dimensional monotone map $a_{n+1} = g(a_n)$. This yields the threshold in closed form: $1 - a_0 = d_{\mathrm{critical}}\,(1 + \ln(1 + 1/d_{\mathrm{critical}}))$, or explicitly in terms of the lower branch $W_{-1}$ of the Lambert W function. We prove a sharp dichotomy. For $d_m \le d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ the cascade halts with limiting load $a_0 + d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ at criticality and surviving fraction $1/(1 + d_{\mathrm{critical}})$. For $d_m > d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ a complete outage occurs in finitely many steps.

entries.name: On a Conjecture About the Sombor Index of Graphs
entries.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and edge set $E(G)$. A graph invariant for $G$ is a number related to the structure of $G$ which is invariant under the symmetry of $G$}. The Sombor and reduced Sombor indices of $G$ are two new graph invariants defined as $SO(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{d_G(u)^2 + d_G(v)^2}$ and $SO_{red}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{\big(d_G(u)-1\big)^2 + \big(d_G(v)-1\big)^2}$, respectively, where $d_G(v)$ is the degree of the vertex $v$ in $G$. We denote by $H_{n,ν}$ the graph constructed from the star $S_n$ by adding $ν$ edge(s), $0\leq ν\leq n-2$, between a fixed pendent vertex and $ν$ other pendent vertices. Réti et al. [T. Réti, T Došlić and A. Ali, On the Sombor index of graphs, \textit{Contrib. Math.} \textbf{3} (2021) 11--18] proposed a conjecture that the graph $H_{n,ν}$ has the maximum Sombor index among all connected $ν$-cyclic graphs of order $n$, where $0\leq\,ν\leq n-2$. In some earlier works the validity of this conjecture was proved for $ν\leq 5$. In this paper we confirm that this conjecture is true, when $ν= 6$. The Sombor index in the case that the number of pendent vertices is less than or equal to $n - ν- 2$ is investigated and the same results are obtained for the reduced Sombor index. Some relationships between Sombor, reduced Sombor and first Zagreb indices of graphs are also obtained.

entries.name: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
entries.abstract: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930. We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.

entries.name: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
entries.abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.

entries.name: De Rham logarithmic classes and Tate conjecture
entries.abstract: We introduce the definition of De Rham logarithmic classes. We show that the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle of a smooth algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero is logarithmic and conversely that a logarithmic class of bidegree $(d,d)$ is the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle (of codimension $d$). We also give for smooth algebraic varieties over a $p$-adic field an analytic version of this result. We deduce from the analytic case the Tate conjecture for smooth projective varieties over fields of finite type over $\mathbb Q$.

entries.name: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
entries.abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomassé. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.

entries.name: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite holes
entries.abstract: Let $n\geq 3$, $λ\in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $n$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with ${\rm Ric}_h > λ$. In this paper, we construct, for each given $ε>0$, a sequence of $(n+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(M_{i} ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_ε,d_ε) $ with ${\rm Ric}_{g_i} > λ$, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_ε) \leq ε$, and $X_ε$ is homeomorphic to the space obtained by removing an infinite number of balls from $X$. Hence $X_ε$ has dense boundary with an infinite number of connected components. Moreover, $X_ε$ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. This generalizes Hupp-Naber-Wang's result (arxiv: 2308.03909) from $4$-dimensional case to the general case of dimension $n\geq 3$. Our construction differs from that of Hupp-Naber-Wang. In their approach, Hupp-Naber-Wang considered doing an infinite number of blow-ups on the local complex surface structure of $X$, thus relying on the $4$-dimensional condition. However, our method involves removing an infinite number of balls from $X$, allowing us to construct in the general case of dimensions greater than or equal to $3$. As a corollary, we provide a solution to an open problem posed by Naber in the $3$-dimensional case.

entries.name: Resolving Gilbert's Conjecture: Dimensional Dependencies in Hardy Spaces Valued in Clifford Modules
entries.abstract: This article provides a thorough investigation into Gilbert's Conjecture, pertaining to Hardy spaces in the upper half-space valued in Clifford modules. We explore the conjecture proposed by Gilbert in 1991, which seeks to extend the classical principle of representing real $L^p$ functions on the real line as boundary values of Hardy holomorphic functions to higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces valued in any Clifford module. We present a complete resolution to this conjecture, demonstrating that its validity is contingent upon the dimension $n$, specifically holding true when \(n \not\equiv 6, 7 \mod 8\) and failing otherwise. The pivotal discovery that Gilbert's conjecture can be reformulated as a set of algebraic conditions is underscored in this work. To navigate these conditions, we employ a novel strategy that leverages the octonions, revealing their instrumental role in addressing issues related to Clifford modules and spinors. This innovative approach not only provides explicit realization through the generalization of the Hilbert transform to the Riesz transform but also establishes a significant advancement in the understanding of Hardy spaces within higher dimensions.

entries.name: Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions
entries.abstract: We enumerate the numbers $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324)$ of 1324-avoiding $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ inversions for all $k$ and $n \geq (k+7)/2$. The result depends on a structural characterization of such permutations in terms of a new notion of almost-decomposability. In particular, our enumeration verifies half of a conjecture of Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson, according to which $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324) \leq \mathrm{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)$ for all $n$ and $k$. Proving also the other half would improve the best known upper bound for the exponential growth rate of the number of $1324$-avoiders from $13.5$ to approximately $13.002$.

entries.name: Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
entries.abstract: A long-standing Conjecture of S. Negami states that a connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane. It is known that the Conjecture is equivalent to the fact that \emph{the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ has no finite planar cover}. We prove three theorems showing that the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ admits no planar cover with certain structural properties, and that the minimal planar cover of $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ (if it exists) must be $4$-connected.

entries.name: Degenerate symplectic fixed points and Gromov-Witten invariants
entries.abstract: We establish a connection between Gromov--Witten invariants and the number of fixed points of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on closed rational symplectic manifolds, without assuming nondegeneracy, via deformed Hamiltonian spectral invariants. We obtain a Hamiltonian fixed point estimate involving Gromov--Witten invariants with one point insertion under an explicit minimum-area hypothesis. We propose three conjectures about Hamiltonian fixed point estimate and prove them for every generalized flag manifold $X=G/P$ equipped with a rational Kähler form. We extend Schwarz's quantum cuplength to deformed quantum cuplength for symplectic periods and use it to obtain estimates on monotone symplectic manifolds admitting nonzero mixed Gromov--Witten invariants. We use the quantum-factorization estimate to recover the Fano toric case of Givental's symplectic fixed-point theorem. Finally, a graded spectral-carrier argument gives uniform fixed-point bounds on negatively monotone manifolds.

entries.name: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
entries.abstract: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $β$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $β$.

entries.name: A geometric perspective on Amitsur's conjecture
entries.abstract: Amitsur proved that Severi--Brauer varieties associated with cyclic algebras of the same degree are birationally equivalent whenever their Brauer classes generate the same cyclic subgroup. We give a geometric proof of this result by constructing explicit birational maps in homogeneous coordinates and using Galois descent.

entries.name: Equivalent bounded confidence processes
entries.abstract: In the bounded confidence model the opinions of a set of agents evolve over discrete time steps. In each round an agent averages the opinion of all agents whose opinions are at most a certain threshold apart. Here we assume that the opinions of the agents are elements of the real line. The details of the dynamics are determined by the initial opinions of the agents, i.e. a starting configuration, and the mentioned threshold -- both admitting uncountably many possibilities. Recently it was conjectured that for each starting configuration the set of thresholds can be partitioned into a finite number of intervals such that the evolution of opinions does not depend on the precise value of the threshold within one of the intervals. So, we may say that, given a starting configuration of initial opinions, there is only a finite number of equivalence classes of bounded confidence processes (and an algorithm to compute them). Here we systematically study different notions of equivalence. Under our broadest notion of equivalence we can also get rid of the initial starting configuration and end up with a finite number of equivalent bounded confidence processes for each given (finite) number of agents. This allows to precisely study the occurring phenomena for small numbers of agents without the jeopardy of missing interesting cases by performing numerical experiments. We exemplarily study the freezing time, i.e. number of time steps needed until the process stabilizes, and the degree of fragmentation, i.e. the number of different opinions that survive once the process has reached its final state.

entries.name: Topology, Hyperbolicity, and the Shafarevich Conjecture for Complex Algebraic Varieties
entries.abstract: This survey presents recent developments concerning the Shafarevich conjecture, non-abelian Hodge theories, hyperbolicity, and the topology of complex algebraic varieties, as well as the interplay among these areas. More precisely, we present the main ideas and techniques involved in the linear versions of the following conjectures: the Shafarevich conjecture, the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture, Kollár's conjecture on the holomorphic Euler characteristic, the de Oliveira-Katzarkov-Ramachandran conjecture, and Campana's nilpotency conjecture. In addition, we discuss characterizations of the hyperbolicity of complex quasi-projective varieties via representations of their fundamental groups, together with the generalized Green-Griffiths-Lang conjecture in the presence of a big local system.

entries.name: Gödel-Tarski Translation for Constructive Logics with Transitive Closure
entries.abstract: We introduce the semantically-defined constructive propositional dynamic logics of regular programs $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$, respectively extending the basic constructive modal logic $\sf CK$ and its Wijesekera-style variant $\sf WK$. Using translations between our logics and $\sf PDL$, we show that both $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$ are {\sc ExpTime}-complete and enjoy an exponential-size finite model property. In particular, their diamond-free fragment, restricted to a single atomic program and its reflexive transitive closure is already {\sc ExpTime}-complete, thereby settling the conjecture of Afshari et al. By embedding $\sf CS4$ and $\sf WS4$ into our logics, we show their validity problems are also in {\sc ExpTime}, improving the previously known {\sc NExpTime} upper bound obtained via finite model arguments.

entries.name: $\boldsymbol{2}$-Neighbor Bootstrap Percolation on Odd Graphs
entries.abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on a graph $G$ is a vertex-activation process that begins with a set of initially active vertices. In each subsequent round, every inactive vertex having at least $r$ active neighbors becomes active. Denote by $m(G,r)$ the minimum number of initially active vertices required for the activation process to spread to all remaining vertices of $G$. In this article, we consider the odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{O}_k\) and the bipartite odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{B}_k\), and prove that $m(\mathbbmsl{O}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+3k+2)/4\rceil$ and $m(\mathbbmsl{B}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+2k+3)/2\rceil$. The first formula confirms the quadratic-growth conjecture proposed in 2021 by Grippo, Pastine, Torres, Valencia-Pabon, and Vera.

entries.name: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
entries.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For central division $F$-algebras $L$ of fixed degree $n$, the double quotients $L^\times\backslash L_E^\times/L^\times$ are identified with a common topological space $\widehatΞ_E$. Each $L$ gives a convolution product $*_E^L$ on the space ${\mathcal M}_E$ of compactly supported measures on $\widehatΞ_E$. The first conjecture asserts that this product is independent of $L$. I prove it for split $E$ and, for every $E$, in degrees $1,2,3,4,6$. The second part of the article defines geometric Hecke operators $T_D^L$ for finite étale divisors $D$ of ${\mathbb P}^1_F$ disjoint from the level divisor, and identifies their convolution measures $μ_D^L\in{\mathcal M}_E$. The second conjecture asserts that these measures are independent of $L$.

entries.name: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
entries.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-Kähler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.

entries.name: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
entries.abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.

entries.name: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
entries.abstract: A polyhex is a connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, joined edge to edge, where each cell has area one. Kurz conjectured an upper bound for the area of the convex hull of a polyhex, after the corresponding problem for squares was solved. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells has area at most one sixth of the ceiling of $n^2+14n/3$, and that for every n this value is attained by a path made of three straight runs of nearly equal length. This proves the conjecture of Kurz and improves his bound by 1/6 when n is divisible by 3. The proof bounds the hull of the cell centres and three of its widths with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The upper bound is formalised in the Lean 4 proof assistant with the Mathlib library. We also show that for every n the extremal polyhex is unique up to rotation, reflection and translation, which an exhaustive search had confirmed for at most 12 cells. The proof of uniqueness was generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz, and it is also formalised in Lean.

entries.name: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
entries.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.

entries.name: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
entries.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $Δ\ge750$ satisfies the Borodin--Kostochka inequality $χ(G)\le\max\{ω(G),Δ-1\}$, conjectured for all $Δ\ge9$. Reed (1999) established the inequality for $Δ\ge10^{14}$, and Liu, Sun, Wang and Zeng (2026) lowered the threshold to $5.3\times10^6$. To extend a random partial colouring over large cliques, we find repeated colours using adaptively chosen vertex-disjoint stars and apply Hall's theorem to the available colour lists. We verify the required probability bounds by rational and interval arithmetic with directed rounding.

entries.name: On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
entries.abstract: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.

entries.name: The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
entries.abstract: We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. We also prove that the intersection of two Grothendieck noncommutative $\cM$-bimodules is also Grothendieck. These answer several open problems in the literature.

entries.name: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
entries.abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.

entries.name: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
entries.abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity.
