We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

entries.name: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
entries.abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_τ:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Zτ)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_τ(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_τ$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given. In particular, we resolve a conjecture of Luo and Wei (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2022).

entries.name: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
entries.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.

entries.name: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
entries.abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

entries.name: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
entries.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

entries.name: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers -- A simple Introduction
entries.abstract: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. We give an elementary introduction to the subject.

entries.name: Sharp integral Ricci pinching on manifolds with positive total scalar curvature
entries.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a closed connected Riemannian three-manifold with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$, and assume that $M$ is not diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We prove the sharp integral Ricci pinching inequality $$\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{6}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2.$$ Moreover, equality holds if and only if $(M,g)$ is locally isometric to $\mathbb{S}^2(a)\times\mathbb{R}$ for some $a>0$. By the same method, we prove $\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{12}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2$ on closed four-manifolds with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$ that have a finite cover with positive first Betti number, and we provide a new proof of Gursky's inequality. We also show that the corresponding inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq 5$, and we give a metric on $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1$ that disproves a conjecture of Ge, Li and Lian.

entries.name: Local Limits and Structures of Nearest-Predecessor Random Graphs
entries.abstract: We study the two-sided nearest-predecessor graph on $[n]$, where vertices arrive in a uniformly random order and each new vertex connects to its nearest earlier vertex on each side. We construct an infinite graph on $\mathbb{Z}$ from i.i.d. continuous insertion times and prove quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence to it almost surely. The limit is almost surely one-ended and recurrent. We resolve an open problem of Ponomarenko by proving that the maximum degree is asymptotic in probability to $\log n/\log(3/2)$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain the probability generating function and a CLT for the number of edges crossing the boundary of $[n]$ in the infinite limit. We also study the $K$-nearest-predecessor graph, in which each new vertex attaches to its $K$ nearest earlier vertices without regard to side. For every fixed $K\geq1$, we construct the infinite limit, prove almost sure quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence, and show that it is almost surely connected, one-ended, and recurrent, as well as nonplanar when $K\geq2$.

entries.name: Rayleigh's conjecture for clamped plates in dimensions four and five
entries.abstract: In 1877, Lord Rayleigh conjectured that the disk minimizes the fundamental frequency of a clamped plate of prescribed area. We prove the higher-dimensional conjecture in dimensions four and five by establishing a sharp comparison between the first clamped-plate eigenvalue and the square of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue on the same domain. The proof uses a nonlinear transformation built from the ball eigenfunctions. A local identity keeps all terms of the Hessian. Exact coefficient inequalities and bounds for the infinite remainders establish positivity, while a weak formulation handles sign changes and critical sets. We characterize equality in the volume inequality and identify an obstruction to this transformation in dimension six.

entries.name: Evidence Toward a Conjecture in List Recoverability of Folded Reed--Solomon Codes
entries.abstract: This paper investigates the list-recoverability of folded Reed--Solomon codes and provides new evidence toward a recent conjecture. Chen--Zhang (STOC 2025) established that for any $\ell,a \ge 2$ and $L = \ell^a - 1$, if a folded Reed--Solomon code of rate $R$ is $(ρ,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, then $ρ\leq \frac{L+1-\ell}{L+1}(1-\frac{aR}{a-1}).$ It is conjectured that this upper bound is tight. We provide two pieces of evidence concerning this conjecture. First, we prove that explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes of rate arbitrarily close to $\tfrac{a-1}{a+\ell-2}$ are $(0,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, which confirms the conjecture in the special case $ρ=0$ and $\ell=2$. Second, we show that for any $R\in(0,\tfrac{a-1}{a})$, there are rates arbitrarily close to $R$ at which attaining the conjectured bound requires exponentially large alphabets. This mirrors the phenomenon observed by Alrabiah--Guruswami--Li (SODA 2024), where achieving the generalized Singleton bound in the list-decoding setting also necessitates exponential alphabet size.

entries.name: Square-zero preservers and tracial states on C*-algebras
entries.abstract: We show that a $C^*$-algebra $A$ of dimension at least two has no tracial states if and only if, for every complex normed space $E$, each bounded symmetric bilinear map $V:A\times A\to E$ with $V(x,x)=0$ for every square-zero $x\in A$ factors through the Jordan product, that is, $V(x,y)=S((xy+yx)/2)$ for some bounded linear map $S:A\to E$ and all $x,y\in A$. The factor $S$ is unique and $\|S\|=\|V\|$. Moreover, applying this bilinear result, we show that $A$ has no tracial states if and only if every bounded square-zero-preserving linear surjection $φ:A\to B$ onto a nonzero Banach algebra with a bounded approximate identity factors as $φ=WJ$, where $J:A\to B$ is a bounded Jordan homomorphism and $W:B\to B$ is a bounded invertible linear centralizer. Likewise, $A$ has no tracial states if and only if every spectrally bounded linear surjection $φ:A\to B$ onto a nonzero semisimple Banach algebra with a bounded approximate identity admits such a factorization. In both cases, the factors are unique and $J$ induces a bounded Jordan isomorphism $A/\kerφ\to B$. In particular, when $φ$ is unital, the factorization reduces to $φ=J$, which settles Mathieu's square-zero conjecture for nonscalar domains and answers the related question on spectrally bounded surjections.

entries.name: Diffusivity and metric exponents for slightly supercritical percolation in high dimensions
entries.abstract: It is a classical fact that random walk on the infinite supercritical Bernoulli $p$-percolation cluster on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ converges to Brownian motion with some diffusivity $σ(p)$, and that the graph metric on the infinite cluster has order $μ(p) \|\cdot\|$ at large scales for some constant $μ(p)$ known as the time constant. We compute the near-critical asymptotics of the two quantities in high dimensions, showing that \begin{align*} σ^2(p) \asymp (p-p_c)^2 \qquad \text{ and } \qquad μ(p) \asymp \frac{1}{\sqrt{p-p_c}} \end{align*} for all $p>p_c$. Our results concerning the diffusivity confirm a conjecture of Biskup (2011). We also compute the asymptotic critical probabilities of slabs in the same regime, showing that $p_c( \mathbb{Z}^{d-1} \times \{0,\ldots,n\}) - p_c(\mathbb{Z}^{d}) \asymp n^{-2}$ as $n\to \infty$.

entries.name: Maximal sections of the cube
entries.abstract: We prove the folklore conjecture on maximal central sections of the cube in every dimension and codimension. The maximizing sections are exactly the products of diagonals of disjoint coordinate blocks whose sizes differ by at most one. This determines the sharp volume in the cases left open by Ball's 1989 bounds. In fixed dimensions, the logarithmic volume deficit controls both the direction and the displacement of an affine section linearly, with optimal exponent. We also obtain the sharp uniform bound on projection densities for independent real random variables with bounded densities.

entries.name: $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property
entries.abstract: Let $(E, P)$, $(E', P')$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{C}$ with marked $p$-torsion points; a marked isogeny is an isogeny sending $P$ to $P'$. We show the marked isogeny relation is interpretable in $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and has strict infinite chains. It follows that $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property, which confirms a special case of the stable fields conjecture.

entries.name: The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds
entries.abstract: We prove the Tate conjecture for non-CM and non-ordinary abelian fourfolds over positive characteristic function fields. Combining our previous works (2512.00687 and 2608.28651), this establishes the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finitely generated fields. Along the way, we classify the $l$-adic monodromy of abelian fourfolds in characteristic $p$ via mixed characteristic lifts and methods from convergent and overconvergent crystalline monodromy, and show that Zarhin's minuscule weights conjecture holds for abelian varieties up to dimension 4. These enable us to prove a characteristic $p$ variant of the Mumford--Tate conjecture for most abelian fourfolds, and reduce the Tate conjecture to Markman's results on the Hodge conjecture.

entries.name: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
entries.abstract: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Ampère equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.

entries.name: No coexistence in the two-type Richardson model when one side is stronger than the other
entries.abstract: We study the two-type Richardson model in two dimensions. We prove that there is no coexistence of the two species when their infection rates are different, establishing a conjecture of H{ä}ggstr{ö}m and Pemantle from 1997. In our proof we analyze a second order approximation of the infected region and use a Mermin--Wagner style argument to push the strong type out of the weak one.

entries.name: Signed Admissible Regions and 2-adic Area Obstructions for Perfect Triangles
entries.abstract: A perfect triangle is a triangle whose sides, medians and area are all integers; whether one exists is an open problem. We study Buchholz's rational parametrization of triangles with two rational medians on the whole $(θ,φ)$-plane, allowing the generated side lengths to be negative. We factor its Heron polynomial $H(θ,φ)$ into ten explicit factors and show that the points whose componentwise absolute values form a triangle are exactly those with $H>0$; the points giving positive side lengths directly form three open quadrilaterals, one of which is the region used by Buchholz and Rathbun. Every triangle with two rational medians arises from sixteen signed parameter points, given by explicit rational functions. Rational area forces $H$ to be a square in $\mathbb{Q}_2$, and the valuation and the unit part of $H$ yield parity and modulo-8 conditions in three valuation ranges. Since a triangle is excluded as soon as one of its sixteen parameter points fails a test, these conditions exclude infinite families of signed admissible parameters, including non-integral ones. The conditions are necessary only and do not settle the existence of perfect triangles.

entries.name: Generic Strong Regularity and the Branson--Gover Conjecture
entries.abstract: On each closed smooth manifold of even dimension $2N\ge 4$, we prove that the Branson--Gover detour operators are strongly regular in every degree $k-1$, $1\le k<N$, on a $C^\infty$-open dense set of Riemannian metrics. Consequently, every de Rham cohomology class of positive degree below the middle dimension has a unique conformal harmonic representative for these metrics. On a connected manifold, the critical scalar GJMS operator has only constants in its kernel on an open dense set of conformal structures modulo diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity, as conjectured by Canzani, Gover, Jakobson, and Ponge. The proof computes the principal symbol of a reduced metric Hessian that accounts for the motion of the kernel through a Green operator.

entries.name: A one-third bound for domination in cubic graphs of girth at least six
entries.abstract: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $S$ has a neighbor in $S$. The domination number $γ(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set of $G$. In 2010, Verstraëte conjectured that every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$ and girth at least six satisfies $γ(G)\le n/3$. More recently, Dorbec and Henning established this bound under the additional assumption that $G$ contains neither a $7$-cycle nor an $8$-cycle. We prove Verstraëte's conjecture in full. As a corollary, we settle the $C_4$-free case of Kostochka's conjecture, which asserts that the same bound holds for all cubic bipartite graphs.

entries.name: A sharp threshold in the Li--Lin open problem
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study positive solutions to the problem \begin{equation*} -Δu = |x|^{-s_2}u^{2^*(s_2)-1} - \la |x|^{-s_1}u^{p-1} \quad \text{in }\Om, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partial\Om, \end{equation*} where $\Om\subset\R^N$ ($N\ge 3$) is a bounded domain with $0\in\partial\Om$, $0\le s_1<s_2<2$, $2^*(s)=\frac{2(N-s)}{N-2}$, $2^*(s_2)<p<2^*(s_1)$, and $\la>0$. This is the Li--Lin open problem \cite{LL} in the form studied by Cerami, Zhong, and Zou \cite{CZZ} and by Tang and Tang \cite{TT1}. Assume that $\partial\Om$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $0$ with a leading term of homogeneity $1+α$, and set $θ=\frac{(N-2)(2^*(s_1)-p)}{2}$. We prove that a solution exists for every $\la>0$ if $θ>α$ and the $α$-mean curvature of $\partial\Om$ at $0$ is negative, whereas $\la^*=\sup\{\la>0:\text{a solution exists}\}$ is finite if $θ\leα$, without any curvature assumption. For $α=1$, this removes the restriction to almost every $\la$ in \cite[Theorem 1.6]{CZZ}, answers a question of Zou \cite{Z}, and disproves the conjecture in \cite[Remark 1.7]{TT1}. The proofs rely on a scale-invariant estimate uniform in $\la$, a Hadamard-type identity for the half-space extremal and a localized Pohozaev identity combined with sharp decay estimates. Notably, no regularity of $\partial\Om$ is required away from $0$.

entries.name: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
entries.abstract: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. Finally, we give a new formulation of Conjecture (E) using the connected descent sets.

entries.name: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
entries.abstract: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor implies the conjecture for the general fiber. As an application, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for Enriques surfaces in every integral curve class.

entries.name: On the quaternionic Goldberg conjecture
entries.abstract: We prove a quaternionic Kähler analogue of the Goldberg conjecture, namely: Let $(M^8,g,Ω)$ denote a compact $8$-manifold endowed with an $\mathrm{Sp}(2)\mathrm{Sp}(1)$-structure defined by a closed $4$-form $Ω$. If the metric $g$ is Einstein with non-negative scalar curvature then it is quaternionic Kähler i.e. $Ω$ is parallel. In fact we prove a slightly stronger result allowing for the scalar curvature to be negative under a suitable pinching condition by the square norm of the intrinsic torsion.

entries.name: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
entries.abstract: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the André-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.

entries.name: Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments
entries.abstract: Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings. This model specializes to the partial matching model for the mixed moments of continuous $q$-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we consider the corresponding multivariate moments and prove that their minimal numerators have nonnegative coefficients up to an explicit sign.

entries.name: Normalized Weyl Energy and the Differential Topology of Four-Manifolds
entries.abstract: The Weyl functional $\int_M\|W_g\|^2\,dμ_g$ plays an important role in four dimensional conformal geometry. Using this functional, Chang, Gursky, and Zhang introduced an invariant of an admissible conformal class and a smooth invariant of the underlying manifold obtained by taking the infimum over all such classes. We use a normalization in which both invariants, denoted by $β(M,c)$ and $β(M)$, take values in $[0,1)$. We prove that every admissible four-manifold $M$ with $β(M)$ sufficiently close to $1/2$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$ up to reversal of orientation. At $β(M)=1/2$, this result and the conformal characterization of the Fubini--Study class confirm Conjecture~1.1 of Chang, Gursky, and Zhang. Among admissible four-manifolds with indefinite intersection form, we prove the corresponding stability of the diffeomorphism type of $S^2\times S^2$ near $2/3$. For the one- and two-point blow-ups of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we show that $β(M)$ lies strictly above the respective topological lower bounds of $2/3$ and $23/30$. These results lead us to ask whether $1$ is the only accumulation point of the values of $β(M)$ and whether, among simply connected admissible four-manifolds, $β(M)$ determines the diffeomorphism type up to reversal of orientation.

entries.name: Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants
entries.abstract: We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. For $uv+h(X_1)+\cdots+h(X_m)=0$, where the $X_i$ are disjoint triples of variables and $m\ge 2$, both series are transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. When $m=2$, we express the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity in terms of a period of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero. This gives an explicit seven-dimensional hypersurface over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with transcendental Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity and transcendental $F$-signature.

entries.name: A martingale proof of simultaneous convex and smooth renorming
entries.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to Problem 198 of Guirao, Montesinos, and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~90], also formulated by Pisier [\emph{Martingales in Banach Spaces}, Cambridge University Press (2016), p.~461]. Given equivalent norms with convexity of power type $p$ and smoothness of power type $q$, respectively, we construct a single equivalent norm with both properties using finite dyadic martingales. It can be chosen arbitrarily close to the given smooth norm in multiplicative distortion and preserves all linear symmetries shared by the two initial norms. The case $p=q=2$ with group invariance answers Problem 3.6 of Cabello Sánchez, Ferenczi, and Randrianantoanina [São Paulo J. Math. Sci. \textbf{16} (2022), 406--458].

entries.name: Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem
entries.abstract: We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $λ> 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $λ> 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.

entries.name: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
entries.abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urbański in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to choose a single pair of potential coefficients that controls both possible separating gaps. The dimension formula remains valid after excluding trivially singular matrices.

entries.name: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
entries.abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\geκ$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $κ$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $κ$. If $κ>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.

entries.name: The spectrum of codegree Turán densities of 3-graphs
entries.abstract: The \emph{minimum codegree} $δ_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Turán density} $γ(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $δ_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $α\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Turán density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_α$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $γ(\mathcal{F}')>α$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_α$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Turán spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independently of us.) We also consider \emph{positive codegree Turán density}, defined analogously by taking the minimum only over $(k-1)$-sets contained in at least one edge. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c<1$ such that, for every integer $k\geq3$, every real number in $[c,1)$ is the positive codegree Turán density of a $k$-graph family. This is done by presenting a construction with a relatively short proof, without optimising the value of $c$.

entries.name: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
entries.abstract: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calderón-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.

entries.name: The optimal exponent in the Erdős--Fuchs theorem for $k$-fold sums
entries.abstract: Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer. For an infinite set $A$ of nonnegative integers and a real number $x\ge0$, let $r_k(A,x)$ be the number of $k$-tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in A^k$ satisfying $a_1+\cdots +a_k\le x$. In this paper, we prove that $r_k(A,x)=cx+o(x^{(1-1/k)^2})$ is impossible for any real number $c>0$. The exponent $(1-1/k)^2$ is best possible for $k\ge3$ by a recent result of Guo and Yan. Moreover, we obtain a mean-square estimate of $r_k(A,x)-cx$ and confirm a conjecture of Chen and Tang for every $k\ge3$.

papers.name: On a Conjecture About the Sombor Index of Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and edge set $E(G)$. A graph invariant for $G$ is a number related to the structure of $G$ which is invariant under the symmetry of $G$}. The Sombor and reduced Sombor indices of $G$ are two new graph invariants defined as $SO(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{d_G(u)^2 + d_G(v)^2}$ and $SO_{red}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{\big(d_G(u)-1\big)^2 + \big(d_G(v)-1\big)^2}$, respectively, where $d_G(v)$ is the degree of the vertex $v$ in $G$. We denote by $H_{n,ν}$ the graph constructed from the star $S_n$ by adding $ν$ edge(s), $0\leq ν\leq n-2$, between a fixed pendent vertex and $ν$ other pendent vertices. Réti et al. [T. Réti, T Došlić and A. Ali, On the Sombor index of graphs, \textit{Contrib. Math.} \textbf{3} (2021) 11--18] proposed a conjecture that the graph $H_{n,ν}$ has the maximum Sombor index among all connected $ν$-cyclic graphs of order $n$, where $0\leq\,ν\leq n-2$. In some earlier works the validity of this conjecture was proved for $ν\leq 5$. In this paper we confirm that this conjecture is true, when $ν= 6$. The Sombor index in the case that the number of pendent vertices is less than or equal to $n - ν- 2$ is investigated and the same results are obtained for the reduced Sombor index. Some relationships between Sombor, reduced Sombor and first Zagreb indices of graphs are also obtained.

papers.name: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
papers.abstract: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930. We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.

papers.name: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
papers.abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.

papers.name: De Rham logarithmic classes and Tate conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the definition of De Rham logarithmic classes. We show that the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle of a smooth algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero is logarithmic and conversely that a logarithmic class of bidegree $(d,d)$ is the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle (of codimension $d$). We also give for smooth algebraic varieties over a $p$-adic field an analytic version of this result. We deduce from the analytic case the Tate conjecture for smooth projective varieties over fields of finite type over $\mathbb Q$.

papers.name: Functional weak convergence of stochastic integrals for moving averages and continuous-time random walks
papers.abstract: There is an extensive theory of weak convergence for moving averages and continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) with respect to Skorokhod's M1 and J1 topologies. Here we address the fundamental question of how this translates into functional limit theorems in the M1 or J1 topology for stochastic integrals driven by these processes. As an important application, we provide weak approximation results for general SDEs driven by time-changed Lévy processes. Such SDEs and their associated fractional Fokker--Planck--Kolmogorov equations are central to models of anomalous diffusion in statistical physics. Our results yield a rigorous functional characterisation of these as continuum limits of the underlying models driven by CTRWs. With regard to strictly M1 convergent moving averages and correlated CTRWs, it turns out that the convergence of stochastic integrals can fail decidedly and fundamental new challenges arise compared to the J1 setting. Nevertheless, we identify natural classes of integrand processes for which there is M1 convergence of the stochastic integrals. We also show that these results are flexible enough to yield functional limit theorems in the M1 topology for certain stochastic delay differential equations driven by moving averages.

papers.name: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomassé. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.

papers.name: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite holes
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 3$, $λ\in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $n$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with ${\rm Ric}_h > λ$. In this paper, we construct, for each given $ε>0$, a sequence of $(n+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(M_{i} ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_ε,d_ε) $ with ${\rm Ric}_{g_i} > λ$, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_ε) \leq ε$, and $X_ε$ is homeomorphic to the space obtained by removing an infinite number of balls from $X$. Hence $X_ε$ has dense boundary with an infinite number of connected components. Moreover, $X_ε$ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. This generalizes Hupp-Naber-Wang's result (arxiv: 2308.03909) from $4$-dimensional case to the general case of dimension $n\geq 3$. Our construction differs from that of Hupp-Naber-Wang. In their approach, Hupp-Naber-Wang considered doing an infinite number of blow-ups on the local complex surface structure of $X$, thus relying on the $4$-dimensional condition. However, our method involves removing an infinite number of balls from $X$, allowing us to construct in the general case of dimensions greater than or equal to $3$. As a corollary, we provide a solution to an open problem posed by Naber in the $3$-dimensional case.

papers.name: Resolving Gilbert's Conjecture: Dimensional Dependencies in Hardy Spaces Valued in Clifford Modules
papers.abstract: This article provides a thorough investigation into Gilbert's Conjecture, pertaining to Hardy spaces in the upper half-space valued in Clifford modules. We explore the conjecture proposed by Gilbert in 1991, which seeks to extend the classical principle of representing real $L^p$ functions on the real line as boundary values of Hardy holomorphic functions to higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces valued in any Clifford module. We present a complete resolution to this conjecture, demonstrating that its validity is contingent upon the dimension $n$, specifically holding true when \(n \not\equiv 6, 7 \mod 8\) and failing otherwise. The pivotal discovery that Gilbert's conjecture can be reformulated as a set of algebraic conditions is underscored in this work. To navigate these conditions, we employ a novel strategy that leverages the octonions, revealing their instrumental role in addressing issues related to Clifford modules and spinors. This innovative approach not only provides explicit realization through the generalization of the Hilbert transform to the Riesz transform but also establishes a significant advancement in the understanding of Hardy spaces within higher dimensions.

papers.name: Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions
papers.abstract: We enumerate the numbers $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324)$ of 1324-avoiding $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ inversions for all $k$ and $n \geq (k+7)/2$. The result depends on a structural characterization of such permutations in terms of a new notion of almost-decomposability. In particular, our enumeration verifies half of a conjecture of Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson, according to which $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324) \leq \mathrm{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)$ for all $n$ and $k$. Proving also the other half would improve the best known upper bound for the exponential growth rate of the number of $1324$-avoiders from $13.5$ to approximately $13.002$.

papers.name: Well-posedness and long-time behavior for self-consistent Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equations with general potentials
papers.abstract: We study the well-posedness, steady states and long time behavior of solutions to Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation with external confinement potential and nonlinear self-consistent interactions. Our analysis introduces newly characterized conditions on the interaction kernel that ensure the local asymptotic stability of the unique steady state. Compared to previous works on this topic, our results allow for large, singular and non-symmetric interactions. As a corollary of our main results, we show exponential decay of solutions to the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation in dimension $3$, for low regularity initial data. In the repulsive case, the result holds in strongly nonlinear regimes (i.e. for arbitrarily small Debye length). Our techniques rely on the design of new Lyapunov functionals based on hypocoercivity and hypoellipticity theories. We use norms which include part of the interaction kernel, and carefully mix ``macroscopic quantities based''--hypocoercivity with ``commutators based''--hypocoercivity.

papers.name: Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
papers.abstract: A long-standing Conjecture of S. Negami states that a connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane. It is known that the Conjecture is equivalent to the fact that \emph{the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ has no finite planar cover}. We prove three theorems showing that the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ admits no planar cover with certain structural properties, and that the minimal planar cover of $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ (if it exists) must be $4$-connected.

papers.name: A Computational Study for Solving Decision-Dependent Robust Problems as Bilevel Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: Both bilevel and robust optimization are established fields of mathematical optimization and operations research. However, only until recently, the similarities in their mathematical structure has neither been studied theoretically nor exploited computationally. Based on the recent results by Goerigk et al. (2025), this paper is the first one that provides an extensive computational study for solving strictly robust optimization problems with decision-dependent uncertainty sets as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. If the uncertainty set can be dualized, the respective bilevel techniques to obtain a single-level reformulation are very similar compared with the classic dualization techniques used in robust optimization but lead to larger single-level problems to be solved. Our numerical study shows that this usually leads to larger computation times. For the more challenging case of decision-dependent uncertainty sets represented by mixed-integer linear models, one cannot apply classic dualization techniques from robust optimization. Thus, we compare the presented bilevel approach with an established method from the literature, which is based on quantified mixed-integer linear programs. Our numerical results indicate that, for the problem class of decision-dependent robust optimization problems with mixed-integer linear uncertainty sets, the bilevel approach performs better in terms of computation times.

papers.name: Fourier transform of nonlinear images of self-similar measures: quantitative aspects
papers.abstract: This paper relates to the Fourier decay properties of images of self-similar measures $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^k$ under nonlinear smooth maps $f \colon \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}$. For example, we prove that if the linear parts of the similarities defining $μ$ commute and the graph of $f$ has non-vanishing Gaussian curvature and $κ_2 > k/2$, then the Fourier dimension of the image measure is at least $\frac{2(2κ_2 - k)}{4 + 2κ_* - k}$, where $κ_2$ is the lower correlation dimension of $μ$ and $κ_*$ is the Assouad dimension of the support of $μ$. Under some additional assumptions on $μ$, we use recent breakthroughs in the fractal uncertainty principle to obtain further improvements for the decay exponents. We give several applications to nonlinear arithmetic of self-similar sets $F$ in the line. For example, we prove that if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (\sqrt{65} - 5)/4 = 0.765\dots$ then the arithmetic product set $F \cdot F = \{ xy : x,y \in F \}$ has positive Lebesgue measure, while if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (-3 + \sqrt{41})/4 = 0.850\dots$ then $F \cdot F \cdot F$ has non-empty interior. One feature of the above results is that they do not require any separation conditions on the self-similar sets.

papers.name: When majority rules, minority loses: bias amplification of gradient descent
papers.abstract: Despite growing empirical evidence of bias amplification in machine learning, its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. We develop a formal framework for majority-minority learning tasks, showing how standard training can favor majority groups and produce stereotypical predictors that neglect minority-specific features. Assuming population and variance imbalance, our analysis reveals three key findings: (i) the close proximity between ``full-data'' and stereotypical predictors, (ii) the dominance of a region where training the entire model tends to merely learn the majority traits, and (iii) a lower bound on the additional training required. Our results are illustrated through experiments in deep learning for tabular and image classification tasks.

papers.name: Degenerate symplectic fixed points and Gromov-Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between Gromov--Witten invariants and the number of fixed points of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on closed rational symplectic manifolds, without assuming nondegeneracy, via deformed Hamiltonian spectral invariants. We obtain a Hamiltonian fixed point estimate involving Gromov--Witten invariants with one point insertion under an explicit minimum-area hypothesis. We propose three conjectures about Hamiltonian fixed point estimate and prove them for every generalized flag manifold $X=G/P$ equipped with a rational Kähler form. We extend Schwarz's quantum cuplength to deformed quantum cuplength for symplectic periods and use it to obtain estimates on monotone symplectic manifolds admitting nonzero mixed Gromov--Witten invariants. We use the quantum-factorization estimate to recover the Fano toric case of Givental's symplectic fixed-point theorem. Finally, a graded spectral-carrier argument gives uniform fixed-point bounds on negatively monotone manifolds.

papers.name: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $β$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $β$.

papers.name: The Solver's Paradox for SAT
papers.abstract: We show in Rocq that every circuit verifier $v$ determines a formula $ψ_v$ whose satisfiability is $v$'s acceptance of its own diagonal claim: a satisfiability predicate thus behaves like a provability predicate. Every solver represented in the language misclassifies its own diagonal instance, and every verifier misjudges its own diagonal claim. We distinguish our result from (i) the refuters of Chen et al. (2024), which produce from the description of a solver an instance it gets wrong, and (ii) the refuter of Gutfreund et al. (2007) for efficient SAT solvers, which needs a hardness hypothesis and a simulation. Here the refuter is purely syntactic, and it separates evaluation of the language from its own expressions, not SAT from a resource-bounded class. The identity behind the fixed point uses no property of quotation; its reading as self-reference depends on the coding, and an injective recoding flips the branch. A truth table decides $ψ_v$ only from outside the language. Written inside, it is brute force: it settles the claim from above and has a diagonal instance of its own. This yields an unconditional certification hierarchy with tower growth, a quadratic lower bound on every internal evaluator, and an exponential lower bound on brute force.

papers.name: A geometric perspective on Amitsur's conjecture
papers.abstract: Amitsur proved that Severi--Brauer varieties associated with cyclic algebras of the same degree are birationally equivalent whenever their Brauer classes generate the same cyclic subgroup. We give a geometric proof of this result by constructing explicit birational maps in homogeneous coordinates and using Galois descent.

papers.name: On the connectedness of a minimizing cluster's boundary
papers.abstract: We verify that an isoperimetric minimizing cluster on a simply connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with at most one end always has connected boundary. In particular, the boundary of a single-bubble isoperimetric minimizer on such manifolds must be connected, and hence all isoperimetric sets and their complements must be connected. This is demonstrably false without the simple connectedness assumption or the restriction on the number of ends.

papers.name: Equivalent bounded confidence processes
papers.abstract: In the bounded confidence model the opinions of a set of agents evolve over discrete time steps. In each round an agent averages the opinion of all agents whose opinions are at most a certain threshold apart. Here we assume that the opinions of the agents are elements of the real line. The details of the dynamics are determined by the initial opinions of the agents, i.e. a starting configuration, and the mentioned threshold -- both admitting uncountably many possibilities. Recently it was conjectured that for each starting configuration the set of thresholds can be partitioned into a finite number of intervals such that the evolution of opinions does not depend on the precise value of the threshold within one of the intervals. So, we may say that, given a starting configuration of initial opinions, there is only a finite number of equivalence classes of bounded confidence processes (and an algorithm to compute them). Here we systematically study different notions of equivalence. Under our broadest notion of equivalence we can also get rid of the initial starting configuration and end up with a finite number of equivalent bounded confidence processes for each given (finite) number of agents. This allows to precisely study the occurring phenomena for small numbers of agents without the jeopardy of missing interesting cases by performing numerical experiments. We exemplarily study the freezing time, i.e. number of time steps needed until the process stabilizes, and the degree of fragmentation, i.e. the number of different opinions that survive once the process has reached its final state.

papers.name: Topology, Hyperbolicity, and the Shafarevich Conjecture for Complex Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: This survey presents recent developments concerning the Shafarevich conjecture, non-abelian Hodge theories, hyperbolicity, and the topology of complex algebraic varieties, as well as the interplay among these areas. More precisely, we present the main ideas and techniques involved in the linear versions of the following conjectures: the Shafarevich conjecture, the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture, Kollár's conjecture on the holomorphic Euler characteristic, the de Oliveira-Katzarkov-Ramachandran conjecture, and Campana's nilpotency conjecture. In addition, we discuss characterizations of the hyperbolicity of complex quasi-projective varieties via representations of their fundamental groups, together with the generalized Green-Griffiths-Lang conjecture in the presence of a big local system.

papers.name: Stochastic Deep Learning: A Probabilistic Framework for Modeling Uncertainty in Structured Temporal Data
papers.abstract: I propose a novel framework that integrates stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with deep generative models to improve uncertainty quantification in machine learning applications involving structured and temporal data. This approach, termed Stochastic Latent Differential Inference (SLDI), embeds an Itô SDE in the latent space of a variational autoencoder, allowing for flexible, continuous-time modeling of uncertainty while preserving a principled mathematical foundation. The drift and diffusion terms of the SDE are parameterized by neural networks, enabling data-driven inference and generalizing classical time series models to handle irregular sampling and complex dynamic structure. A central theoretical contribution is the co-parameterization of the adjoint state with a dedicated neural network, forming a coupled forward-backward system that captures not only latent evolution but also gradient dynamics. I introduce a pathwise-regularized adjoint loss and analyze variance-reduced gradient flows through the lens of stochastic calculus, offering new tools for improving training stability in deep latent SDEs. My paper unifies and extends variational inference, continuous-time generative modeling, and control-theoretic optimization, providing a rigorous foundation for future developments in stochastic probabilistic machine learning.

papers.name: Kantorovich Distance via Spanning Trees: Properties and Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study optimal transport between probability measures supported on the same finite metric space, where the ground cost is a distance induced by a weighted connected graph. Building on recent work showing that the resulting Kantorovich distance can be expressed as a minimization problem over the set of spanning trees of this underlying graph, we investigate the implications of this reformulation on the construction of an optimal transport plan and a dual potential based on the solution of such an optimization problem. In this setting, we derive an explicit formula for the Kantorovich potential in terms of the imbalanced cumulative mass (a generalization of the cumulative distribution in R) along an optimal spanning tree solving such a minimization problem, under a weak non-degeneracy condition on the pair of measures that guarantees the uniqueness of a dual potential. Our second contribution establishes the existence of an optimal transport plan that can be computed efficiently by a dynamic programming procedure once an optimal spanning tree is known. Finally, we propose a stochastic algorithm based on simulated annealing on the space of spanning trees to compute such an optimal spanning tree. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed approach for optimal transport on finite metric spaces.

papers.name: The non-ergodic Host-Kra-Ziegler structure theorem for $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions via measurable selections
papers.abstract: We establish a non-ergodic version of the Host--Kra--Ziegler structure theorem for measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions. Our argument reduces the non-ergodic case to the ergodic theorem (for $d\ge 2$ due to Candela and Szegedy) via a measurable selection procedure. We also establish a non-ergodic vertical nilcharacter version of our main result. The non-ergodic version of the Host--Kra--Ziegler structure theorem is a key input in the companion paper by the second author and Fraczyk classifying point processes (i.e. random subsets) of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ whose law is invariant under the group $\mathrm{ASL}_d(\mathbb{Z})$ of affine transformations.

papers.name: Gödel-Tarski Translation for Constructive Logics with Transitive Closure
papers.abstract: We introduce the semantically-defined constructive propositional dynamic logics of regular programs $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$, respectively extending the basic constructive modal logic $\sf CK$ and its Wijesekera-style variant $\sf WK$. Using translations between our logics and $\sf PDL$, we show that both $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$ are {\sc ExpTime}-complete and enjoy an exponential-size finite model property. In particular, their diamond-free fragment, restricted to a single atomic program and its reflexive transitive closure is already {\sc ExpTime}-complete, thereby settling the conjecture of Afshari et al. By embedding $\sf CS4$ and $\sf WS4$ into our logics, we show their validity problems are also in {\sc ExpTime}, improving the previously known {\sc NExpTime} upper bound obtained via finite model arguments.

papers.name: On the Chevalley-Bass number of a field
papers.abstract: We give upper and lower bounds on the Chevalley-Bass number of a field of characteristic zero, whenever this quantity is well-defined. We also describe an algorithm which computes the Chevalley-Bass number of a field, provided its maximal abelian subextension is known. As a primary application, we improve the value of a constant related to exponential Diophantine equations.

papers.name: $\boldsymbol{2}$-Neighbor Bootstrap Percolation on Odd Graphs
papers.abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on a graph $G$ is a vertex-activation process that begins with a set of initially active vertices. In each subsequent round, every inactive vertex having at least $r$ active neighbors becomes active. Denote by $m(G,r)$ the minimum number of initially active vertices required for the activation process to spread to all remaining vertices of $G$. In this article, we consider the odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{O}_k\) and the bipartite odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{B}_k\), and prove that $m(\mathbbmsl{O}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+3k+2)/4\rceil$ and $m(\mathbbmsl{B}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+2k+3)/2\rceil$. The first formula confirms the quadratic-growth conjecture proposed in 2021 by Grippo, Pastine, Torres, Valencia-Pabon, and Vera.

papers.name: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For central division $F$-algebras $L$ of fixed degree $n$, the double quotients $L^\times\backslash L_E^\times/L^\times$ are identified with a common topological space $\widehatΞ_E$. Each $L$ gives a convolution product $*_E^L$ on the space ${\mathcal M}_E$ of compactly supported measures on $\widehatΞ_E$. The first conjecture asserts that this product is independent of $L$. I prove it for split $E$ and, for every $E$, in degrees $1,2,3,4,6$. The second part of the article defines geometric Hecke operators $T_D^L$ for finite étale divisors $D$ of ${\mathbb P}^1_F$ disjoint from the level divisor, and identifies their convolution measures $μ_D^L\in{\mathcal M}_E$. The second conjecture asserts that these measures are independent of $L$.

papers.name: Involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction
papers.abstract: We determine all involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction that extend the involution of the original $*$-algebra. We also find all algebra isomorphisms between the resulting Cayley doubles that extend the identity automorphism of the original $*$-algebra, and consequently classify the resulting $*$-algebras up to such $*$-algebra isomorphisms. As applications, we show that Cayley doubles of algebras without zero divisors admit exactly one additional extension of the original involution in the 2-torsion-free case and none otherwise, prove that the classical Cayley-Dickson involution is the unique scalar involution, and obtain a classification of the $*$-algebras arising from $\mathbb{R}$ up to dimension 4.

papers.name: Nilpotent quiver varieties with multiplicities and symmetrisable crystals
papers.abstract: We construct analogues of Nakajima's nilpotent quiver varieties for quivers with multiplicities, by developing new stability conditions for framed nilpotent quiver representations with multiplicities and exploiting their interplay with Hecke correspondences. Using these new quiver varieties, we extend Saito's geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals of irreducible highest-weight representations of Kac--Moody algebras from the symmetric to the symmetrisable case.

papers.name: Multilevel limits of spiked random matrix corners processes
papers.abstract: We consider the largest eigenvalues of submatrices of the classical Gaussian random matrices with a finite rank spike in the critical BBP regime. We show that they converge to a multilevel interlacing particle system whose lowest level is the Airy$_β$ point process. Our construction and scaling limits extend in a natural way to non-classical $β>0$.

papers.name: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
papers.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-Kähler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.

papers.name: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
papers.abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.

papers.name: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
papers.abstract: A polyhex is a connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, joined edge to edge, where each cell has area one. Kurz conjectured an upper bound for the area of the convex hull of a polyhex, after the corresponding problem for squares was solved. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells has area at most one sixth of the ceiling of $n^2+14n/3$, and that for every n this value is attained by a path made of three straight runs of nearly equal length. This proves the conjecture of Kurz and improves his bound by 1/6 when n is divisible by 3. The proof bounds the hull of the cell centres and three of its widths with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The upper bound is formalised in the Lean 4 proof assistant with the Mathlib library. We also show that for every n the extremal polyhex is unique up to rotation, reflection and translation, which an exhaustive search had confirmed for at most 12 cells. The proof of uniqueness was generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz, and it is also formalised in Lean.

papers.name: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

papers.name: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.

papers.name: Bias Correction and Inference for Panel Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: We develop a large-$n$, large-$T$ theory for the unsmoothed fixed-effects quantile regression estimator that allows for serially correlated panel data. An exact rank-score identity for the profiled criterion, with a convexity argument, delivers the leading incidental parameter bias of the slope estimator, of order $T^{-1}$, in closed form, paralleling Hahn and Newey (2004) for smooth nonlinear panel models. When $n$ and $T$ grow at the same rate, the estimator is asymptotically normal but in general not centred, and conventional intervals are invalid. In stationary panels whose dependence decays geometrically or polynomially, with $n/T$ bounded, serial correlation changes the structure of this bias: the long-run variance of the quantile score enters it, and feedback from past errors to current regressors adds a term that can bias the estimator even at the median. A split-panel jackknife with contiguous half-panels removes the bias, whereas one with interleaved half-panels does not in general, and a cluster-robust variance estimator, clustered by individual, yields valid inference. Under independence over time, the admissible growth of $n$ relative to $T$, up to $n=o(T^3)$, depends on the regularity of the conditional error densities, and the jackknife is valid throughout this range.

papers.name: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $Δ\ge750$ satisfies the Borodin--Kostochka inequality $χ(G)\le\max\{ω(G),Δ-1\}$, conjectured for all $Δ\ge9$. Reed (1999) established the inequality for $Δ\ge10^{14}$, and Liu, Sun, Wang and Zeng (2026) lowered the threshold to $5.3\times10^6$. To extend a random partial colouring over large cliques, we find repeated colours using adaptively chosen vertex-disjoint stars and apply Hall's theorem to the available colour lists. We verify the required probability bounds by rational and interval arithmetic with directed rounding.

papers.name: On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
papers.abstract: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.

papers.name: The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
papers.abstract: We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. We also prove that the intersection of two Grothendieck noncommutative $\cM$-bimodules is also Grothendieck. These answer several open problems in the literature.

papers.name: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.

papers.name: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
papers.abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

papers.name: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
papers.abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_τ:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Zτ)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_τ(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_τ$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given. In particular, we resolve a conjecture of Luo and Wei (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2022).

papers.name: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.

papers.name: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
papers.abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

papers.name: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

papers.name: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers -- A simple Introduction
papers.abstract: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. We give an elementary introduction to the subject.

papers.name: On the solution of a question for meromorphic functions sharing three values IM and a fourth value CM in the complex plane
papers.abstract: In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a Möbius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

papers.name: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
papers.abstract: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.

papers.name: Sharp integral Ricci pinching on manifolds with positive total scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a closed connected Riemannian three-manifold with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$, and assume that $M$ is not diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We prove the sharp integral Ricci pinching inequality $$\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{6}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2.$$ Moreover, equality holds if and only if $(M,g)$ is locally isometric to $\mathbb{S}^2(a)\times\mathbb{R}$ for some $a>0$. By the same method, we prove $\mathrm{vol}(g)\int_M |\mathrm{Ric}^{\circ}|^2 \mathrm{d}v \geq \frac{1}{12}\left(\int_M R \mathrm{d}v\right)^2$ on closed four-manifolds with $\int_M R \mathrm{d}v>0$ that have a finite cover with positive first Betti number, and we provide a new proof of Gursky's inequality. We also show that the corresponding inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq 5$, and we give a metric on $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^1$ that disproves a conjecture of Ge, Li and Lian.

papers.name: Local Limits and Structures of Nearest-Predecessor Random Graphs
papers.abstract: We study the two-sided nearest-predecessor graph on $[n]$, where vertices arrive in a uniformly random order and each new vertex connects to its nearest earlier vertex on each side. We construct an infinite graph on $\mathbb{Z}$ from i.i.d. continuous insertion times and prove quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence to it almost surely. The limit is almost surely one-ended and recurrent. We resolve an open problem of Ponomarenko by proving that the maximum degree is asymptotic in probability to $\log n/\log(3/2)$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain the probability generating function and a CLT for the number of edges crossing the boundary of $[n]$ in the infinite limit. We also study the $K$-nearest-predecessor graph, in which each new vertex attaches to its $K$ nearest earlier vertices without regard to side. For every fixed $K\geq1$, we construct the infinite limit, prove almost sure quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence, and show that it is almost surely connected, one-ended, and recurrent, as well as nonplanar when $K\geq2$.

papers.name: Rayleigh's conjecture for clamped plates in dimensions four and five
papers.abstract: In 1877, Lord Rayleigh conjectured that the disk minimizes the fundamental frequency of a clamped plate of prescribed area. We prove the higher-dimensional conjecture in dimensions four and five by establishing a sharp comparison between the first clamped-plate eigenvalue and the square of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue on the same domain. The proof uses a nonlinear transformation built from the ball eigenfunctions. A local identity keeps all terms of the Hessian. Exact coefficient inequalities and bounds for the infinite remainders establish positivity, while a weak formulation handles sign changes and critical sets. We characterize equality in the volume inequality and identify an obstruction to this transformation in dimension six.

papers.name: Evidence Toward a Conjecture in List Recoverability of Folded Reed--Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the list-recoverability of folded Reed--Solomon codes and provides new evidence toward a recent conjecture. Chen--Zhang (STOC 2025) established that for any $\ell,a \ge 2$ and $L = \ell^a - 1$, if a folded Reed--Solomon code of rate $R$ is $(ρ,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, then $ρ\leq \frac{L+1-\ell}{L+1}(1-\frac{aR}{a-1}).$ It is conjectured that this upper bound is tight. We provide two pieces of evidence concerning this conjecture. First, we prove that explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes of rate arbitrarily close to $\tfrac{a-1}{a+\ell-2}$ are $(0,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, which confirms the conjecture in the special case $ρ=0$ and $\ell=2$. Second, we show that for any $R\in(0,\tfrac{a-1}{a})$, there are rates arbitrarily close to $R$ at which attaining the conjectured bound requires exponentially large alphabets.
